updates.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November. Fable shares a base model with Mythos and adds cyber and biology safeguards for use. Organizations can apply for Mythos through verification programs. Anthropic says output runs up to 30% faster than with 5.1. Fable 5.2 costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
updates.whyCare: The release adds a high-capability model for harder technical work and a separate access path for sensitive domains. Compare its speed, cost, and safeguards with your current model before routing high-stakes tasks.
updates.before: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 were the previous generation. Teams had no 5.2 option for demanding technical work.
updates.after: Fable 5.2 is available with cyber and biology safeguards. Organizations can apply for Mythos 5.2 through Anthropic's Cyber or Life Sciences Verification Programs.
updates.learn: Test Fable 5.2 on your technical workloads before rerouting traffic. Compare completed-task cost and latency with Opus 5.5 or open models. Apply for Mythos if your organization needs its sensitive-domain capabilities.
updates.architectureImplication: Route demanding technical work to Fable only after task-level evaluation. Keep Mythos behind Anthropic's verification controls for cyber or biomedical research, and compare model cost with Opus 5.5, hosted alternatives, and open models.

updates.title: AWS adds single-shot and passage-only retrieval to Bedrock Knowledge Bases
updates.whatChanged: AWS expanded Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base's AgenticRetrieveStream API on 9 November. Setting maxAgentIteration to 0 returns passages without a foundation-model call; 1 runs one retrieval and generates an answer; 2–5 retain agentic retrieval with iterative planning.
updates.whyCare: You can set retrieval effort per request: return source passages, answer a direct question with one retrieval, or keep iterative search for complex questions. This can cut model calls and latency on simple queries while preserving multi-step retrieval for harder ones.
updates.before: Teams could use the separate Retrieve API for passage-only access, but AgenticRetrieveStream did not offer single-shot RAG.
updates.after: One AgenticRetrieveStream request can return passages only at maxAgentIteration=0, run single-shot RAG at 1, or keep agentic retrieval at 2–5.
updates.learn: Route direct questions to one iteration and passage-only workflows to zero. Test the iteration cap on multi-part queries, then compare latency, model calls, and answer quality with your existing retrieval path.

updates.architectureImplication: Applications can use one managed API for passage retrieval, basic RAG, and multi-step RAG. Keep custom orchestration or the separate Retrieve API where you need different model, ranking, filtering, or serving controls.
